title: Non-flat free-boundary minimal disks in the superball
plain: In a round ball the only free-boundary minimal disks are flat slices through the centre (Nitsche). The superball x^4+y^4+z^4 <= 1 has nine flat ones, cut by its mirror planes. Is there also one that is not flat? A natural candidate has threefold symmetry about the diagonal (1,1,1). Such a symmetric disk cannot be flat: the only plane invariant under both symmetries is x+y+z=0, and it meets the boundary orthogonally only where xyz=0.
math: For $p>2$ let $B_p=\{|x|^p+|y|^p+|z|^p\le1\}$. Decide whether $B_4$ (more generally $B_p$) contains an embedded minimal disk $\Sigma$ with $\partial\Sigma\subset\partial B_p$, meeting $\partial B_p$ orthogonally, that is not contained in a plane. Specifically, show that there is one invariant under the rotation by $2\pi/3$ about the axis $\mathbb R(1,1,1)$ and under $v\mapsto-v$.
review_note: Open; equivariant free-boundary min-max (Ketover) is the natural route, but producing a disk with the required symmetry is not routine.
refs: J.C.C. Nitsche, Stationary partitioning of convex bodies, Arch. Rational Mech. Anal. 89 (1985)
M. Grüter and J. Jost, On embedded minimal disks in convex bodies, Ann. Inst. H. Poincaré Anal. Non Linéaire 3 (1986)
D. Ketover, Equivariant min-max theory, arXiv:1612.08692
